daily_reality.summary: Oral and maxillofacial surgeons treat the entire craniomaxillofacial complex — mouth, jaws, face, skull, and neck. Most work in private practices or outpatient surgery centers; hospital-based surgeons handle trauma and complex reconstructive cases.
typical_tasks: Evaluate patients using X-rays, CT scans, CBCT, and MRIs for diagnosis
Perform wisdom tooth extractions (most common procedure)
Place dental implants and perform bone grafting
Orthognathic surgery (Le Fort I, BSSO) for jaw realignment
Treat facial trauma — fractures of mandible, maxilla, zygoma, orbit
Excise tumors and cysts of the jaws and oral cavity
Administer local anesthesia, IV sedation, and general anesthesia
Perform cleft lip/palate repairs and craniofacial reconstruction
TMJ surgery and temporomandibular disorder management
Facial cosmetic procedures — rhinoplasty, facial rejuvenation
daily_reality.seasonality: Steady year-round demand. Slight increase in wisdom tooth extractions during summer (students on break) and holiday periods. Trauma cases spike during holidays and weekends.

regulatory.summary: Dual-licensed under both dental and often medical boards. Regulated by state dental boards with additional permits for anesthesia and surgical procedures. Board certification through ABOMS is voluntary but strongly encouraged.

key_laws.name: State Dental Practice Acts
key_laws.description: Each state's dental board regulates OMS licensure, scope of practice, and anesthesia permits

key_laws.name: ABOMS Board Certification
key_laws.description: Only certifying board for OMS in the US — Qualifying Exam (300 questions, 11 areas) + Oral Certifying Exam (144 minutes, 12 cases)

key_laws.name: CODA Accreditation Standards
key_laws.description: Commission on Dental Accreditation sets standards for OMS residency programs

key_laws.name: DEA Registration
key_laws.description: Required for prescribing controlled substances (opioids, sedatives)

requirements: DMD or DDS degree from CODA-accredited dental school (4 years)
Many programs include MD degree (6-year integrated track)
State dental license (pass NBDE/INBDE + state clinical exam)
Anesthesia/sedation permit from state dental board
ABOMS board certification (recommended but not required)

regulatory.continuing_education: 50-60 CME hours per biennial cycle; ABOMS requires yearly Certification Maintenance activities including Annual Registration

tools.summary: Highly technology-dependent specialty using advanced imaging (CBCT, CT), virtual surgical planning, 3D printing, and specialized surgical instruments. Digital workflows are transforming the field.

primary_tools.name: CBCT (Cone Beam Computed Tomography)
primary_tools.description: 3D imaging essential for implant planning, impacted teeth assessment, pathology evaluation

primary_tools.name: Planmeca Romexis CMF Surgery
primary_tools.description: Virtual treatment planning for orthognathic surgery, merges CBCT with intraoral scans

primary_tools.name: 3D Systems VSP (Virtual Surgical Planning)
primary_tools.description: Interactive service for simulating procedures with engineers, producing surgical splints

primary_tools.name: Carestream Dental OMS Imaging
primary_tools.description: Imaging platform with prosthetic-driven implant planning and CBCT integration

primary_tools.name: Dolphin Imaging
primary_tools.description: Comprehensive tools for cephalometric analysis, 3D surgical simulation, and treatment planning

primary_tools.name: DEXIS Digital Ecosystem
primary_tools.description: AI-powered platform combining 2D/3D imaging, intraoral scanning, and diagnostics

secondary_tools: DSN Software — AI-assisted CBCT analysis, nerve detection, implant planning
Diagnocat AI — automated CBCT segmentation and 3D STL model generation
Practice management software (Dentrix, Open Dental, Eaglesoft)
3D printers for surgical guides and models
Piezoelectric surgical units for precision bone cutting
Surgical navigation systems for complex cases
pain_points: High cost of CBCT equipment and software licenses
Learning curve for virtual surgical planning platforms
Insurance pre-authorization delays for complex procedures
Integration issues between dental and medical software systems
Maintaining proficiency across rapid technology changes

terminology.summary: Highly specialized surgical vocabulary blending dental, medical, and surgical terminology. Heavy use of abbreviations for procedures, anatomy, and clinical findings.

terms.BSSO: Bilateral Sagittal Split Osteotomy — mandibular correction procedure
terms.Le Fort I/II/III: Classification of maxillary fractures and osteotomy levels
terms.ORIF: Open Reduction Internal Fixation — fracture repair with plates/screws
terms.IV sedation: Intravenous sedation (hallmark of OMS anesthesia training)
terms.bone graft: Autogenous, allograft, or synthetic bone for ridge augmentation
terms.impaction: Tooth embedded in bone (soft tissue vs. partial vs. full bony)
terms.mandibulectomy: Surgical removal of part/all of the mandible (tumor cases)
terms.intermaxillary fixation: Wiring jaws together (IMF) for fracture healing

career_psychology.summary: One of the longest and most demanding training paths in healthcare (10-14 years post-college). High compensation but significant stress. Over 91% report career satisfaction, though burnout exists especially in residency.
career_path: Optional fellowship (head & neck oncology, craniofacial, cosmetic)
Associate in established practice or hospital (1-3 years)
Practice owner / partner in private OMS practice
Academic OMS — program director, department chair
fears: Nerve damage during surgery (inferior alveolar, lingual nerve)
Falling behind on rapidly evolving technology
motivation: Transformative impact on patients' lives (jaw surgery, trauma repair)
High income potential and practice autonomy
Variety of procedures from simple extractions to complex reconstruction
burnout_factors: Extremely long training path (10-14 years after college)
High-stakes procedures with low margin for error
Dealing with complex insurance and pre-authorization
>50% of OMS residents report moderate to severe anxiety

community.summary: Strong professional community centered around AAOMS (9,000+ members, 90%+ of US oral surgeons). Multiple specialty societies, active journal, and state/regional chapters.

associations.name: American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS)
American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (ABOMS)
American College of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (ACOMS)
International Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (IAOMS)

publications.name: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (JOMS)
publications.description: Flagship peer-reviewed journal of the specialty

events: AAOMS Annual Meeting, Scientific Sessions and Exhibition
State and regional OMS society meetings (50 state + 8 regional chapters)

market.summary: Strong job market with high demand driven by aging population, dental implant growth, and trauma care needs. Ranked #6 in Best-Paying Jobs. Over 1,500 active job openings nationwide.
demand_drivers: Growing demand for dental implants (aging population)
Increased access to elective facial surgeries
market_trends: Shift toward digital workflows and virtual surgical planning
AI integration in imaging and treatment planning
Increasing insurance coverage for orthognathic surgery
